review_notes: I read all 245 lines of TaylorCoeff.lean and checked the Mathlib API it relies on: Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/DSlope.lean (dslope_same, dslope_of_ne, dslope_sub_smul_of_ne, pow_sub_smul_iterate_dslope_of_zero), Mathlib/Analysis/Analytic/IsolatedZeros.lean (has_fpower_series_iterate_dslope_fslope, coeff_zero, coeff_iterate_fslope, eq_pow_order_mul_iterate_dslope), Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/Deriv/Mul.lean (deriv_const_mul_field), and Mathlib/Logic/Function/Iterate.lean (Semiconj.iterate_right). I also inspected the sibling residue-calculus files (LaurentCoeff.lean, PrincipalPart.lean, Residue.lean) for repeated coefficient computations. Candidate repetitions within the target are all routine: (i) the pointwise b = z₀ / b ≠ z₀ case splits in dslope_const_mul (82–88), dslope_const (90–95) and dslope_sub_mul (156–166) are routine unfolding of dslope via dslope_same/dslope_of_ne; (ii) the iterate inductions in taylorCoeffAt_congr (76–80), taylorCoeffAt_const_mul (99–103) and taylorCoeffAt_zero_fun (106–108) are one-step unfoldings of taylorCoeffAt_succ (a rfl lemma) and would at most be replaced by a generic iterate/semiconjugacy call (e.g. Function.Semiconj.iterate_right), which is an API-shortening rather than nontrivial repeated mathematics; (iii) taylorCoeffAt_zero_fun (105–108) is a special case of taylorCoeffAt_const_mul (97–103), and taylorCoeffAt_const (110–114) reuses zero_fun, but these are short specialisations. The genuine workhorse identities (dslope_sub_mul, taylorCoeffAt_sub_pow_mul, the Taylor-polynomial coefficient computation hGcoeff and the factorization h1 inside AnalyticAt.exists_taylor_remainder) each occur exactly once. The hterm block in exists_taylor_remainder (216–222) resembles PrincipalPart.eq_principalPart_of_eventuallyEq's hterm (227–232), but those are different coefficient functions (Taylor vs. Laurent) proved from different monomial lemmas, so they are not the same repeated proof. Under the rubric's exclusion of short calculations, routine unfolding, thin wrappers and moved branch code, I found no justified finding. Remaining uncertainty: I could not run Lean, so I did not test whether a semiconjugacy-based or iterate-lifting refactor would compile or would actually shorten the three short inductions; in any case such a refactor would address proof brevity rather than nontrivial repeated reasoning.
